Outcome: Depression cases (lower is better)

## Study A
Found: benefit
Claim: Self-reported vitamin D deficiency status was positively associated with depression.
Sentence: "Significant positive correlations were seen with vitamin D deficiency status and certain chronic conditions such as chronic kidney disease (p = 0.04), depression (p < 0.001), diabetes (p = 0.02), and vitamin D supplement use (p < 0.001)."
Measured as: depression
Population: US adults completing an online questionnaire
Intervention: Self-reported vitamin D deficiency status (exposure, not administered)
Comparator: Adults not reporting vitamin D deficiency
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 1,637
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported

## Study B
Found: no effect
Claim: Dietary vitamin D intake was not significantly associated with risk of depression in the fully adjusted model.
Sentence: "No significant association was found between vitamin D dietary intake and risk of depression in the full-adjusted model (OR: 0.96, 95% CI: 0.62, 1.51)."
Measured as: risk of depression (Beck Depression Inventory-II)
Population: 690 healthy physically active adults (athletes) aged 18-50 in Kashan, Iran
Intervention: Dietary vitamin D intake assessed by 147-item FFQ (tertiles)
Comparator: Lowest tertile of vitamin D intake
Design: cross-sectional study
Sample size: 690
baseline_vitamin_d_status: not_reported
